text: I'm the shift leader at a regional parcel depot and I've got this sealed container of returned electronics that sat by the dock door overnight. Nobody saw it get wet, and the team thinks it stayed dry, but it rained heavily last night, so now I'm not so sure. We could run a moisture scan and it would only take about five minutes, but the lorry driver has a fixed ferry booking, and if we do the scan and make him miss the slot, the customers' refunds get delayed another day. If we just load it and some of the items are wet, then the returns technicians and the customers end up dealing with damaged stock and complaints. I don't know whether to do the quick check or let it go and hope it's fine. What should I do?

I've got a sealed container of returned electronics that may have gotten wet overnight. A moisture scan takes five minutes, but it could make the driver miss his ferry and delay refunds. Should I scan it or load it as is?

I'm a shift leader and need to decide whether to load a sealed container of returned electronics onto the afternoon lorry. It spent the night near the dock door during heavy rain, and we're not sure if it stayed dry. A five-minute moisture scan would tell us, but the driver has a ferry deadline and missing it would delay customer refunds. If we skip the scan and the items are wet, technicians and customers will have to deal with the damage. What's the right call here?

I need help figuring out what to do, and I’m kind of embarrassed to even ask. I live in a small housing co-op, and a while ago I told my adult brother he could stay in my spare room for four months while he starts an apprenticeship. He was really relieved, and he went ahead and gave notice to his landlord and paid a moving deposit that he can’t get back. At the time I honestly thought I could manage it. Since then, my co-op housing charge went up, and I’ve been going over my budget again and again, and if he stays here the way we planned, I’d have to cut my daughter’s after-school care to make it work. That feels wrong, but I also keep thinking about my brother, because he made real plans based on what I said, and if I back out now he may be completely stuck. I haven’t told him any of this yet. Part of me keeps putting it off because I’m afraid that if I say anything now, I’ll ruin everything for him, but I also know that waiting longer probably makes it worse. I don’t know whether I should tell him immediately, try to find some other arrangement, or wait until I have a clearer solution. I just don’t know what I owe him after promising something I now realize I shouldn’t have promised so easily.
